Enum ShapeClipperFillRule

Namespace
ShapeEngine.ShapeClipper
Assembly
ShapeEngine.dll

Filling rules determine which sub-regions of complex polygons are considered "inside". Complex polygons are defined by one or more closed contours; only portions of these contours may contribute to filled regions, so a filling rule is required to decide which sub-regions are treated as inside when performing clipping operations.

Fields

EvenOdd = 0

Even-Odd rule: only sub-regions with odd winding parity are filled.

Negative = 3

Negative rule: only sub-regions with winding counts < 0 are filled.

NonZero = 1

Non-Zero rule: any sub-region with a non-zero winding number is filled.

Positive = 2

Positive rule: only sub-regions with winding counts > 0 are filled.

Examples

Example algorithm (winding number): From a point outside the polygon draw a ray through the polygon. Start with winding number 0. For each contour crossed, increment the winding number if the crossing goes right-to-left relative to the ray, otherwise decrement. Each sub-region gets the current winding number.

Remarks

The supported fill rules are based on winding numbers derived from the orientation of each path:

  • Even-Odd: toggles inside/outside each time a contour is crossed.
  • Non-Zero: considers the sum of winding contributions; non-zero means inside.
  • Positive / Negative: depend on the sign of the winding number.

Notes:

  • The most commonly used rules are Even-Odd and Non-Zero.
  • Reversing a path reverses its orientation (and the sign of winding numbers) but does not affect parity or whether a winding number is zero.
  • Filling rules are required only for clipping operations; they do not affect polygon offsetting.
